stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.

Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They recruited 64 five-year-old children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers then recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group that received no special response

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 300 families. For each one, they recorded the warmth of parenting, as rated by observers and the child's self-esteem score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.48.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group that held the pen between the teeth
The group that held the pen between the lips

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They recruited 84 office workers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They hypothesized that the treatment would affect the severity of depression.

**Participants.** The sample was 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.

**Results.** The group that received therapy: mean depression score = 11. The group on the waiting list: mean depression score = 21. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Does sleep improve memory?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 60 students learned a list of word pairs at 9 p.m. Half were randomly assigned to sleep normally and half to stay awake all night. Twelve hours later, the sleep group recalled a mean of 31 pairs out of 40 and the awake group recalled a mean of 22 (p = 0.01).

**Source B.** Researchers recorded the brain activity of 25 adults in a sleep laboratory after they had learned a maze. The more slow-wave (NREM stage 3) sleep a participant had, the faster that participant completed the maze the next morning (r = +0.55).

**Source C.** A survey of 900 high school students found that those who reported sleeping fewer than six hours on school nights had lower average grades than those who slept eight hours or more. The researchers noted that students who slept less also reported more stress and more hours of paid work.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route?

options.why: Massed practice is study that is crammed into one long session.
A hierarchy is the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones.
Distributed practice is study that is spread out over several sessions.
Correct. The method of loci is the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route.

questions.explanation: The method of loci is the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes grammar?

options.text: The whole system of rules in a language that lets people communicate
options.why: Correct. This is what grammar means.

options.text: The smallest unit of language that carries meaning
options.why: That describes a morpheme.

options.text: The rules by which we get meaning from words and sentences
options.why: That describes semantics.

options.text: The rules for ordering words into sentences
options.why: That describes syntax.

questions.explanation: Grammar is the whole system of rules in a language that lets people communicate.

questions.stem: A slot machine pays out after an unpredictable number of plays. Which schedule of reinforcement is this?

options.why: A fixed-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced.
Correct. A variable-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after an unpredictable number of responses.
A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.
A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.

questions.explanation: A variable-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after an unpredictable number of responses.

questions.stem: During a near-miss in traffic, glands above the kidneys release a hormone that makes the driver's heart race. Which hormone is this?

options.why: Correct. Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.
Ghrelin is the hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger.
Oxytocin is the hormone that promotes bonding, trust and social attachment.
Leptin is the hormone released by fat cells that signals fullness and reduces hunger.

questions.explanation: Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.

questions.stem: A psychologist proposes that people learn to fear snakes easily because ancestors who avoided snakes were more likely to survive. Which approach is the psychologist using?

options.why: Nature is the influence of inherited genetic factors on behavior and mental processes.
Epigenetics is the study of how the environment changes whether genes are expressed without changing the DNA itself.
Correct. The evolutionary perspective is the approach that explains behavior through natural selection of traits that helped ancestors survive and reproduce.
Nurture is the influence of environmental factors, such as upbringing and experience, on behavior and mental processes.

questions.explanation: The evolutionary perspective is the approach that explains behavior through natural selection of traits that helped ancestors survive and reproduce.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness?

options.why: Binge-eating disorder is the eating disorder in which a person repeatedly eats very large amounts and feels distress, without purging afterward.
Bulimia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person binges on food and then makes up for it by vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise.
Correct. Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.
Anorexia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person restricts food to the point of being dangerously underweight, with an intense fear of gaining weight.

questions.explanation: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.

questions.stem: A car's loud beeping stops as soon as the driver fastens the seat belt, so the driver fastens it more quickly in future. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.
Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Correct. Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Positive reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it.

questions.explanation: Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: The walking group recalled more locations. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The type of exercise and memory are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The type of exercise caused the difference in memory
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: Consent is obtained before the study.
Replication is repeating a study.
A placebo is an inactive treatment.
Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: Dan believes that his grades depend on luck and on whether the teacher likes him. Which belief does he hold?

options.why: An internal locus of control is the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions.
Upward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing better.
Correct. An external locus of control is the belief that outcomes are decided by luck, fate or other people.
A dispositional attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to the person's own traits or character.

questions.explanation: An external locus of control is the belief that outcomes are decided by luck, fate or other people.

questions.stem: Can the researchers conclude that conscientiousness score on a personality inventory causes a change in grade point average?

options.text: Yes, because the correlation is not zero
options.why: Any nonzero correlation still leaves the cause unknown.

options.text: Yes, because the sample was large
options.why: A large sample does not turn a correlation into evidence of causation.

options.text: No, because a correlation does not show cause and effect
options.why: Correct. Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

options.text: No, because correlations can only be calculated in experiments
options.why: Correlations are calculated in non-experimental studies.

questions.explanation: Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.stem: After the election result is announced, Tom says, 'I knew all along that she would win,' although he had predicted the opposite. Which bias is this?

options.why: Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.
Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.
Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.
Correct. Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.

questions.explanation: Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.

questions.stem: Omar generally feels that he is a valuable and likeable person. Which term describes this overall feeling?

options.why: Self-efficacy is the belief in one's own ability to succeed at a particular task.
Correct. Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.
Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.
Self-concept is all the thoughts and feelings a person has in answer to the question 'Who am I?'.

questions.explanation: Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: The homeowners asked to sign the petition lived on a road where an accident had recently happened
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The two groups differed in compliance with a large request at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: One group differed from the other in whether a small request came first
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: To remember the term 'hippocampus', Sol links it to a hippo on a campus who never forgets his classes. Which technique is he using?

options.why: Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.
Correct. Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.
Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.
Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.

questions.explanation: Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.why: Experiments also use numerical data.

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Sample size does not determine the research method.
Experiments also test hypotheses.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality?

options.why: Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.
A projective test is a personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings.
Correct. A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.
The self-actualizing tendency is in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential.

questions.explanation: A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.

questions.stem: When Ken trips, he blames the uneven pavement; when a stranger trips, Ken thinks the stranger is clumsy. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Relative deprivation is the feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with.
An optimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors.
Correct. The actor-observer bias is the tendency to explain our own behavior by the situation but other people's behavior by their traits.
The self-serving bias is the tendency to credit our successes to ourselves and blame our failures on outside factors.

questions.explanation: The actor-observer bias is the tendency to explain our own behavior by the situation but other people's behavior by their traits.

questions.stem: After an infection damaged the tiny bones of his middle ear, Arun's hearing was restored with a hearing aid that amplifies sound. Which kind of hearing loss did he have?

options.why: Correct. Conduction deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the eardrum or the bones of the middle ear.
Volley theory is the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies.
Place theory is the theory that we hear different pitches because different sound waves trigger different places on the cochlea's membrane.
Sound localization is the ability to tell where a sound comes from, using differences in timing and loudness between the two ears.

questions.explanation: Conduction deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the eardrum or the bones of the middle ear.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes denial?

options.text: The defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one
options.why: That describes displacement.

options.text: The defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people
options.why: That describes projection.

options.text: The defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior
options.why: That describes rationalization.

options.text: The defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality
options.why: Correct. This is what denial means.

questions.explanation: Denial is the defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality.

questions.stem: Athletes perform poorly when they are either too relaxed or too anxious, and best when moderately excited. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Arousal theory is the theory that people are motivated to keep an ideal level of alertness and stimulation.
Drive-reduction theory is the theory that a physical need creates a state of tension that motivates behavior to reduce it.
Incentive theory is the theory that behavior is pulled by rewards from outside the person.
Correct. The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.

questions.explanation: The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.

questions.stem: Carl's behavior is far outside what people in his culture consider usual or acceptable. Which criterion for a psychological disorder does this meet?

options.why: Correct. Deviation from the social norm is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior differs markedly from what a culture expects.
Dysfunction is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior interferes with daily life, such as work and relationships.
The DSM is the American Psychiatric Association's manual for classifying and diagnosing psychological disorders.
The ICD is the World Health Organization's international system for classifying all diseases, including mental disorders.

questions.explanation: Deviation from the social norm is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior differs markedly from what a culture expects.

questions.stem: A child's parents and teachers meet regularly and work together. In ecological systems theory, this connection is part of which system?

options.why: The chronosystem is in ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child.
The exosystem is in ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace.
The macrosystem is in ecological systems theory, the cultural values, laws and customs that surround a child.
Correct. The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.

questions.explanation: The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes separation anxiety?

options.text: The attachment style in which a child uses the caregiver as a safe base, is upset when the caregiver leaves and is comforted on return
options.why: That describes secure attachment.

options.text: The insecure attachment style in which a child seems indifferent when the caregiver leaves and ignores the caregiver on return
options.why: That describes avoidant attachment.

options.text: The comfort from physical touch that Harlow showed is more important to attachment than feeding
options.why: That describes contact comfort.

options.text: The distress that infants show when a familiar caregiver leaves, which peaks around 13 months
options.why: Correct. This is what separation anxiety means.

questions.explanation: Separation anxiety is the distress that infants show when a familiar caregiver leaves, which peaks around 13 months.

questions.stem: In the middle of laughing at a joke, Viktor suddenly falls asleep. Which sleep disorder does he most likely have?

options.why: Insomnia is a sleep disorder with ongoing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.
Somnambulism is sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep.
Correct. Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep.
Sleep apnea is a sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings.

questions.explanation: Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep.

questions.stem: In people who are blind, the area that normally processes vision responds to touch when they read Braille. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A split brain is the condition in which the two hemispheres cannot communicate because the corpus callosum has been cut.
Correct. Neuroplasticity is the brain's ability to change by reorganizing after damage or building new pathways through experience.
Lesioning is the destruction of a small area of brain tissue to study its function.
An EEG is a recording of the electrical waves that sweep across the brain's surface.

questions.explanation: Neuroplasticity is the brain's ability to change by reorganizing after damage or building new pathways through experience.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession?

options.why: Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.
Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.
Color constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting.
Correct. Apparent movement is the perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession.

questions.explanation: Apparent movement is the perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a schema?

options.text: The changing of an existing schema to fit new information
options.why: That describes accommodation.

options.text: A mental framework that organizes and interprets information
options.why: Correct. This is what a schema means.

options.text: The best or most typical example of a category
options.why: That describes a prototype.

options.text: A mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people
options.why: That describes a concept.

questions.explanation: A schema is a mental framework that organizes and interprets information.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: One group differed from the other in the color of the drinks
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

options.text: The mismatched drinks were served colder than the matching drinks
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The two groups differed in flavor identification at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Which part of a neuron first receives a chemical message from a neighboring neuron?

options.why: The axon is the long fiber that carries the neural impulse away from the cell body toward other cells.
The cell body is the part of the neuron that contains the nucleus and keeps the cell alive.
The synapse is the tiny gap between the sending neuron and the receiving neuron.
Correct. A dendrite is a branching extension of a neuron that receives messages from other neurons.

questions.explanation: A dendrite is a branching extension of a neuron that receives messages from other neurons.

questions.stem: Six dots are drawn as three close pairs, and people see three groups rather than six dots. Which Gestalt principle explains this?

options.why: Figure and ground is the Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background.
Correct. Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.
Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.
Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.

questions.explanation: Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = +0.50. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship with the negative sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes contralateral control?

options.text: The area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension
options.why: That describes Wernicke's area.

options.text: The tendency for each side of the brain to handle certain functions, such as language in the left hemisphere
options.why: That describes hemispheric specialization.

options.text: The arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body
options.why: Correct. This is what contralateral control means.

options.text: The area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production
options.why: That describes Broca's area.

questions.explanation: Contralateral control is the arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care?

options.why: The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.
A meta-analysis is a statistical procedure that combines the results of many studies to reach an overall conclusion.
Cultural humility is a therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view.
Correct. Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.

questions.explanation: Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the exposure therapy that pairs relaxation with a graded series of anxiety-arousing stimuli?

options.why: Biofeedback is the technique of using electronic monitoring to show a person their body's signals so that they can learn to control them.
A token economy is the behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards.
Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.
Correct. Systematic desensitization is the exposure therapy that pairs relaxation with a graded series of anxiety-arousing stimuli.

questions.explanation: Systematic desensitization is the exposure therapy that pairs relaxation with a graded series of anxiety-arousing stimuli.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution?

options.why: Convergent thinking is thinking that narrows the possibilities down to the single best answer.
Divergent thinking is thinking that produces many possible answers to a problem.
Correct. An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution.
A heuristic is a simple thinking shortcut that is fast but can lead to errors.

questions.explanation: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the deep encoding of a word based on its meaning?

options.why: Explicit memory is the memory of facts and experiences that a person can consciously recall and state.
Effortful processing is the encoding that requires attention and conscious effort.
Correct. Semantic encoding is the deep encoding of a word based on its meaning.
Structural encoding is the shallow encoding of a word based on its appearance.

questions.explanation: Semantic encoding is the deep encoding of a word based on its meaning.

questions.stem: From her first weeks, baby Ivy has been calm and easygoing, while her brother was fussy and intense. This difference is one of which of the following?

options.why: Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.
Correct. Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.
Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.
Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.

questions.explanation: Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident. What does this most limit?

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes dialectical behavior therapy?

options.text: The technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones
options.why: That describes cognitive restructuring.

options.text: The therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior
options.why: That describes cognitive-behavioral therapy.

options.text: The pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression
options.why: That describes the cognitive triad.

options.text: The therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder
options.why: Correct. This is what dialectical behavior therapy means.

questions.explanation: Dialectical behavior therapy is the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder.

questions.stem: Red light and blue light differ in color. Which property of the light waves differs?

options.why: Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.
Correct. Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.
The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.
Frequency is the number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch.

questions.explanation: Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.

questions.stem: Seven students took a memory test. Their scores were 4, 9, 9, 6, 19, 13, 10. What is the range of the scores?

options.why: That is the median.
That is the mean.
Correct. Subtract the lowest score from the highest.
That is the highest score.

questions.explanation: In order, the scores are 4, 6, 9, 9, 10, 13, 19. Subtract the lowest score from the highest. The one very high score pulls the mean (10) above the median (9), so the distribution is positively skewed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs?

options.why: Correct. Tardive dyskinesia is the involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs.
An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.
Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.
An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.

questions.explanation: Tardive dyskinesia is the involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs.

questions.stem: An eight-year-old answers the questions that a typical ten-year-old can answer. On Binet's test, ten is the child's what?

options.why: Multiple intelligences is the theory that people have several independent kinds of intelligence, such as musical and interpersonal.
Correct. Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.
The Flynn effect is the steady rise in average intelligence test scores over the generations.
The intelligence quotient is originally, mental age divided by chronological age and multiplied by 100.

questions.explanation: Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.

questions.stem: A researcher sends a questionnaire about sleep habits to 2,000 adults. Which research method is this?

options.why: Replication is the repeating of a study with different participants to see whether the finding holds.
A correlational study is the research method that measures two variables to see how they are related, without manipulating either.
Correct. A survey is the research method of collecting self-reported attitudes or behaviors from a sample by asking questions.
Falsifiability is the quality of a claim that it could be shown to be wrong by evidence.

questions.explanation: A survey is the research method of collecting self-reported attitudes or behaviors from a sample by asking questions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow?

options.why: Free association is the psychodynamic technique in which the client says whatever comes to mind.
Dream interpretation is the psychodynamic technique of analyzing dreams to uncover unconscious wishes and conflicts.
Correct. Person-centered therapy is the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow.
Hypnosis is a state of heightened suggestibility that can help reduce pain and anxiety but does not reliably recover memories.

questions.explanation: Person-centered therapy is the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow.

questions.stem: Afraid of being trapped in a crowd or on a bus, Mr. Diaz has not left his house in six months. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Taijin kyofusho is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly in Japan, marked by fear of offending or embarrassing others.
Panic disorder is the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain.
Social anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations.
Correct. Agoraphobia is the disorder in which a person fears and avoids public places from which escape might be difficult.

questions.explanation: Agoraphobia is the disorder in which a person fears and avoids public places from which escape might be difficult.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the failure to notice that something in the environment has changed?

options.why: Correct. Change blindness is the failure to notice that something in the environment has changed.
A perceptual set is a readiness to perceive something in a particular way because of expectations.
Top-down processing is perception that is guided by experience, expectations and context.
Bottom-up processing is perception that starts with the raw sensory input and builds up to a complete picture.

questions.explanation: Change blindness is the failure to notice that something in the environment has changed.

questions.stem: Just as Rosa drifts off, she feels as if she is falling and jerks awake. Which stage of sleep was she in?

options.why: The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.
REM sleep is the sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles.
REM rebound is the tendency to have more REM sleep after being deprived of it.
Correct. NREM stage 1 is the brief, light first stage of sleep, in which a person may have hypnagogic sensations such as falling.

questions.explanation: NREM stage 1 is the brief, light first stage of sleep, in which a person may have hypnagogic sensations such as falling.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: −0.70, −0.93, −0.61, +0.35. Which coefficient shows the weakest relationship?

options.why: −0.61 is farther from zero.
−0.70 is farther from zero.
Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; +0.35 is closest to zero.
−0.93 is farther from zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. +0.35 is closest to zero.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm?

options.why: Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.
Integrity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate.
Correct. Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.

options.text: Respect for people's rights and dignity
options.why: Respect for people's rights and dignity is the ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices.

questions.explanation: Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.

questions.stem: Each night, Noor writes down three things she is thankful for, and over time she feels happier. Which practice is this?

options.why: Correct. Gratitude is the appreciation of the good things in one's life, the practice of which raises well-being.
Subjective well-being is a person's own evaluation of how happy and satisfied they are with life.
Resilience is the ability to recover and adapt well after stress or hardship.
Posttraumatic growth is the positive psychological change that some people experience after struggling with a very difficult event.

questions.explanation: Gratitude is the appreciation of the good things in one's life, the practice of which raises well-being.

questions.stem: Around age 51, Mrs. Ortiz's menstrual cycles stop permanently. Which term describes this change?

options.why: Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.
Secondary sex characteristics is the nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice.
Menarche is a girl's first menstrual period.
Correct. Menopause is the natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50.

questions.explanation: Menopause is the natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes observational learning?

options.text: Learning by watching others and imitating them
options.why: Correct. This is what observational learning means.

options.text: Learning from seeing the consequences of another person's behavior
options.why: That describes vicarious conditioning.

options.text: Learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it
options.why: That describes latent learning.

options.text: A mental picture of the layout of one's surroundings
options.why: That describes a cognitive map.

questions.explanation: Observational learning is learning by watching others and imitating them.

questions.stem: An expert pool player makes more of her shots when a crowd is watching than when she plays alone. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Group polarization is the strengthening of a group's existing opinions after the members discuss them.
Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.
Correct. Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.
Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.

questions.explanation: Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: Dana pictures the layout of her house to count the windows. Which part of working memory is she using?

options.why: Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.
The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.
The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.
Correct. The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.

questions.explanation: The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are?

options.why: Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.
Generativity versus stagnation is Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work.
Correct. Identity versus role confusion is Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are.
Intimacy versus isolation is Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships.

questions.explanation: Identity versus role confusion is Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes universal emotions?

options.text: The interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels
options.why: That describes cognitive appraisal.

options.text: An event or stimulus that triggers an emotion
options.why: That describes an elicitor.

options.text: The basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures
options.why: Correct. This is what universal emotions means.

options.text: A cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom
options.why: That describes a display rule.

questions.explanation: Universal emotions is the basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures.

questions.stem: Which sense detects the basic qualities of sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus?

options.why: Correct. Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.
Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.
A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.
A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.

questions.explanation: Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a factor other than the independent variable that differs between groups and could explain the results?

options.why: A single-blind procedure is a procedure in which the participants do not know which condition they are in.
Effect size is the measure of how large the difference or relationship found in a study is.
Correct. A confounding variable is a factor other than the independent variable that differs between groups and could explain the results.
The placebo effect is an improvement that results from a person's expectation of a treatment rather than from the treatment itself.

questions.explanation: A confounding variable is a factor other than the independent variable that differs between groups and could explain the results.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive?

options.why: Correct. Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.

questions.stem: Scores on a university entrance test correlate strongly with students' later grades. Which quality does the test have?

options.why: Correct. Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.
Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.
Standardization is the giving and scoring of a test in the same way for everyone, and the comparison of scores with a pretested group.
Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.

questions.explanation: Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the prefrontal cortex?

options.text: The front part of the frontal lobes, which handles executive functions such as planning and self-control
options.why: Correct. This is what the prefrontal cortex means.

options.text: The strip at the rear of the frontal lobes that controls voluntary movements
options.why: That describes the motor cortex.

options.text: The lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement
options.why: That describes the frontal lobes.

options.text: The lobes above the ears, which process sound and help recognize language
options.why: That describes the temporal lobes.

questions.explanation: The prefrontal cortex is the front part of the frontal lobes, which handles executive functions such as planning and self-control.

questions.stem: People who move next to a railway are woken by trains at first but soon sleep through the noise. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A taste aversion is a learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness.
Correct. Habituation is the decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over.
Counterconditioning is the replacing of an unwanted response to a stimulus with a new response, by pairing the stimulus with something pleasant.
Biological preparedness is the inborn readiness to learn some associations, such as taste and nausea, more easily than others.

questions.explanation: Habituation is the decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes informational social influence?

options.text: The strategy of making a large request that will be refused so that a smaller request is more likely to be accepted
options.why: That describes the door-in-the-face technique.

options.text: Persuasion that works through surface cues, such as an attractive or famous speaker
options.why: That describes the peripheral route to persuasion.

options.text: The influence that comes from a person's willingness to accept others' views as evidence about reality
options.why: Correct. This is what informational social influence means.

options.text: Persuasion that works through evidence and logical arguments, which people think about carefully
options.why: That describes the central route to persuasion.

questions.explanation: Informational social influence is the influence that comes from a person's willingness to accept others' views as evidence about reality.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a hallucinogen?

options.text: A drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input
options.why: Correct. This is what a hallucinogen means.

options.text: A drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions
options.why: That describes a stimulant.

options.text: A drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions
options.why: That describes a depressant.

options.text: A drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive
options.why: That describes an opioid.

questions.stem: Researchers find that a person who collapses is helped more quickly when one person is nearby than when a crowd is nearby. What is this finding called?

options.why: Correct. The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.
Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.
Burnout is the physical and emotional exhaustion that results from long-term stress at work.
An industrial-organizational psychologist is a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being.

questions.explanation: The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.

questions.stem: A four-year-old invents a game and organizes her friends to play it. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Trust versus mistrust is Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met.
Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.
Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.
Correct. Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.

questions.explanation: Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: On the way home, Lin remembers that she must stop to buy milk. Which kind of memory is this?

options.why: Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.
Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.
Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.
Correct. Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.

questions.explanation: Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 100 and a standard deviation of 20. About what percentage of scores are above 100?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. A normal distribution is symmetrical, so half the scores lie above the mean.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.

questions.explanation: A normal distribution is symmetrical, so half the scores lie above the mean. (80 and 120 are one standard deviation from the mean; 60 and 140 are two.)

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of the severity of depression

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of the severity of depression.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: The severity of depression was defined as each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The therapy group had lower depression scores. On average, the value was 11 for the group that received therapy and 21 for the group on the waiting list, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The therapy group had lower depression scores. (11 compared with 21).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the treatment affects the severity of depression. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the treatment. The finding illustrates cognitive-behavioral therapy, which reduces depression by changing negative thought patterns (the cognitive triad) and behavior.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Does sleep improve memory?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Sleep improves memory because memories are consolidated during sleep.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, students who slept recalled a mean of 31 of 40 word pairs, compared with 22 for students who stayed awake.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through memory consolidation: during sleep, the hippocampus and cortex strengthen newly encoded memories, so the sleep group stored the word pairs better. Because the study was an experiment with random assignment, sleep can be said to have caused the difference.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, participants who had more slow-wave sleep completed the maze faster the next morning (r = +0.55).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim because NREM stage 3 sleep is linked to strengthening the neural connections formed during learning (long-term potentiation), so more deep sleep goes with better retention of the maze.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
